blocks.p: They went on then until they came to the Delectable Mountains, which belong to the Lord of that hill we spoke of before. So they went up into the mountains to see the gardens and orchards, the vineyards and fountains of water; and there they drank and washed themselves, and ate freely from the vineyards. Now on the tops of these mountains there were shepherds feeding their flocks, standing beside the highway. The pilgrims went over to them, and leaning on their staffs (as weary pilgrims commonly do when they stop to talk with someone along the road), they asked, “Whose Delectable Mountains are these? And whose sheep are these that graze on them?”

v: Up the delectable mountains now they
where shepherds stand, who to them
things that delight, and things that warn and steer;
for pilgrims are kept steady by faith and fear.

blocks.p: “These mountains are Immanuel’s Land,” said the shepherds, “and they are within sight of his city. The sheep are his too, and he laid down his life for them.” [John 10:11]
“Is this the way to the Celestial City?” said Christian.
“You are right on the road.”
“How far is it?”
“Too far for anyone except those who will really get there.”
“Is the way safe or dangerous?”
“Safe for those it is meant to be safe for; but the rebellious will stumble on it.” [Hos. 14:9]
“Is there any relief in this place for pilgrims who are weary and faint on the road?”
“The Lord of these mountains has charged us not to forget to show hospitality to strangers. So all the good of this place is yours.” [Heb. 13:1-2]

I saw also in my dream that when the shepherds saw they were travelers, they asked them questions too, which they answered as they had in other places: Where did you come from? How did you get onto the road? And how have you managed to keep going on it? For few of those who start out for this place ever show their faces on these mountains. But when the shepherds heard their answers, they were pleased, and looked at them very warmly, and said, “Welcome to the Delectable Mountains.”
The shepherds, I say, whose names were Knowledge, Experience, Watchful, and Sincere, took them by the hand and brought them to their tents and gave them a share of what was ready to eat.
“We would like you to stay here a while,” they said, “to get to know us, and even more, to refresh yourselves with the good things of these Delectable Mountains.”
The pilgrims told them they were glad to stay. So they went to bed that night, because it was very late.

Then I saw in my dream that in the morning the shepherds called Christian and Hopeful to come and walk with them on the mountains. So they went out with them and walked a while, with a pleasant view on every side.
“Shall we show these pilgrims some wonders?” the shepherds said to one another.

When they had agreed to do it, they took them first to the top of a hill called Error, which was very steep on its far side, and told them to look down to the bottom. So Christian and Hopeful looked down, and at the bottom they saw several men dashed to pieces by a fall they had taken from the top.
“What does this mean?” said Christian.
“Haven’t you heard of those who were led astray by listening to Hymenaeus and Philetus about the faith of the resurrection of the body?” the shepherds answered. [2 Tim. 2:17-18]
“Yes,” they said.

“Those you see lying dashed to pieces at the bottom of this mountain are the very ones. And they have lain there unburied to this day, as you see, as an example to others to take care how they climb too high, or how near they come to the edge of this mountain.”

Then I saw that they took them to the top of another mountain, whose name is Caution, and told them to look far off. When they did, they saw what they took to be several men walking up and down among the tombs there. They could tell the men were blind, because they kept stumbling over the tombs and could not find their way out from among them.
“What does this mean?” said Christian.
“Didn’t you see, a little below these mountains, a stile that led into a meadow on the left-hand side of this road?” the shepherds answered.
“Yes.”

“From that stile a path leads directly to Doubting Castle, which is kept by Giant Despair. And these men,” pointing to them among the tombs, “once came on pilgrimage, as you are doing now, until they came to that same stile. And because the right road was rough at that point, they chose to leave it for that meadow, and there they were taken by Giant Despair and thrown into Doubting Castle. After they had been kept in the dungeon a while, he finally put out their eyes and led them among those tombs, where he has left them to wander to this very day, so that the saying of the wise man might be fulfilled: ‘Whoever wanders from the way of understanding will come to rest in the company of the dead.’” [Prov. 21:16]
Then Christian and Hopeful looked at each other with tears streaming down, but they said nothing to the shepherds.

Then I saw in my dream that the shepherds took them to another place, down in a hollow, where there was a door in the side of a hill. They opened the door and told them to look in. So they looked in, and saw that it was very dark and smoky inside. They thought they also heard a rumbling noise like fire, and the cries of some who were in torment, and they smelled the smell of brimstone.
“What does this mean?” said Christian.

“This is a side road to hell,” the shepherds told them, “a way that hypocrites go in by: those who sell their birthright, like Esau; those who sell their master, like Judas; those who blaspheme the gospel, like Alexander; and those who lie and deceive, like Ananias and his wife Sapphira.”
“I take it,” said Hopeful to the shepherds, “that every one of these had the look of a pilgrim, as we have now. Didn’t they?”
“Yes, and kept it up a long time too.”
“How far might they have gone on pilgrimage in their day, and yet in spite of that been so miserably thrown away?”
“Some farther than these mountains, and some not so far.”
Then the pilgrims said to each other, “We need to cry out to the Strong One for strength.”
“Yes,” said the shepherds, “and you will need to use it when you have it, too.”
By this time the pilgrims wanted to go on, and the shepherds wanted them to as well; so they walked together toward the end of the mountains.
“Let’s show the pilgrims the gates of the Celestial City from here,” the shepherds said to each other, “if they have the skill to look through our telescope.”
The pilgrims gladly accepted the offer. So the shepherds took them to the top of a high hill called Clear, and gave them their telescope to look through.

They tried to look; but the memory of that last thing the shepherds had shown them made their hands shake, and because of that they could not hold the telescope steady. Still, they thought they saw something like the gate, and also some of the glory of the place. Then they went away and sang this song:

v: And so, by shepherds, secrets are revealed
which from all other men are kept concealed.
Come to the shepherds, then, if you would see
things deep, things hidden, things of mystery.

blocks.p: When they were about to leave, one of the shepherds gave them a set of directions for the road. Another told them to beware of the Flatterer. The third told them to take care not to fall asleep on the Enchanted Ground. And the fourth wished them Godspeed.
So I woke from my dream.
